_provenance.notes: The Alaska Board of Fisheries (BOF) is the regulatory body that sets escapement goals, allocations, and harvest policies for all Alaska state fisheries. It consists of 7 members appointed by the Governor. The BOF operates on a 3-year rotation cycle for different regions. The Board is the key decision-making body — understanding its recent actions is critical to understanding current Alaska fisheries management.

1960s.impact: State authority over fisheries management formalized. ADF&G becomes primary management agency.

1960s.action: First statewide salmon escapement guidelines adopted
1960s.impact: Beginning of escapement-based management — moving away from pure effort control.

1970s.action: Limited entry (CFEC) authorized by Alaska Legislature
1970s.impact: Fundamental restructuring of commercial fishing access. Permits frozen as property rights.

1970s.action: CFEC issues first limited entry permits — salmon fisheries statewide
1970s.impact: 14,900 salmon permits issued. Race to fish ends for permit holders.

1970s.action: Escapement goals formally required for all key salmon fisheries
1970s.impact: Biological basis for management of all commercial salmon fisheries established.

1970s.action: Personal use (dipnet) fishery established on Kenai River
1970s.impact: Recognition of resident Alaskan's subsistence interests in the most valuable run.

1980s.impact: Federal subsistence priority on federal public lands — begins dual-management system.

1980s.action: Copper River sockeye OEG adopted — first Optimal Escapement Goal
1980s.impact: More sophisticated escapement goal framework for high-value fisheries.
Major economic expansion of SEAK/PWS herring sector — right before Exxon Valdez.

1990s.action: BOF adopts escapement goal framework statewide (SEG/OEG/BEG)
1990s.impact: Standardized three-tier escapement goal system for biological sustainability.

1990s.action: Kenai River late-run Chinook SEG adopted: 15,000-30,000
1990s.impact: Science-based management of the most important sport Chinook run.

1990s.action: Yukon River Chinook salmon — first commercial restrictions
1990s.impact: Commercial fishery begins transitioning away from targeting Chinook.

2000s.action: Salmon disaster declarations — BOF authorizes emergency regulations
2000s.impact: First major in-season response to price crash and poor returns simultaneously.

2000s.action: BOF adopts genetic stock identification protocols
2000s.impact: GSI becomes a management tool for in-season stock composition analysis.

2000s.action: Kenai River Chinook ADF&G adopts new sonar program
2000s.impact: DIDSON technology improves daily escapement counting resolution for management.
ADF&G strengthens genetic separation requirements for hatchery programs near wild stocks.

2010s.action: Yukon River Chinook — near-complete commercial closure
2010s.impact: Subsistence-only access; cultural crisis for river communities.

2010s.action: BOF Bristol Bay Sockeye — sockeye escapement goals revised upward
2010s.impact: Higher escapement goals reflect improved understanding of carrying capacity.

2010s.action: Kuskokwim River — KRSMWG (collaborative management working group) established
2010s.impact: Co-management with Yukon Delta tribes — landmark policy change.

2010s.action: BOF Cook Inlet — commercial set net allocation reduction
2010s.impact: Controversial reallocation from commercial to sport fisheries in UCI.

2020s.action: BOF adopts climate change vulnerability assessment framework
2020s.impact: First formal acknowledgment of climate as primary long-term driver in AK fisheries mgmt.

2020s.action: Yukon and Kuskokwim subsistence closures — unprecedented
2020s.impact: First time in history both rivers closed for salmon subsistence. Federal disaster declarations.

2020s.action: BOF adopts adaptive management triggers for Bering Sea crab
2020s.impact: Automatic rebuilding provisions triggered if populations fall below threshold.

2020s.action: Bristol Bay red king crab reopened with minimal TAC (2.31M lbs)
2020s.impact: First BBRKC season since 2020 — carefully managed rebuilding fishery.
